desc:
You are given two binary search trees a and b. Build one new balanced binary search tree that contains every value that occurs in at least one of them. A value present in both trees appears once in the result.

To make the answer unique, take the combined values in increasing order and build the tree with this rule: for any range of the sorted list, the root is the lower middle element (index (lo + hi) / 2 rounded down); the elements before it form the left subtree, the elements after it form the right subtree, built the same way. Return the tree in level-order encoding.

Within one tree all values are distinct. One of the two trees may be empty ([]), but not both.

Tree encoding. A binary tree is written as an integer array in level order. The first entry is the root. After that, the left and right child of every existing node are written in turn, level by level, from left to right. A missing child is written as -1 (real node values are never negative, so -1 cannot be confused with a value). Missing nodes have no children listed, and trailing -1 entries are dropped. The empty tree is [].

For example, [5,2,7,-1,3,6] is the tree whose root 5 has left child 2 and right child 7; node 2 has no left child and right child 3; node 7 has left child 6 and no right child.

Example 1

a = [4,2,6], b = [3,1,5]
Output: [3,1,5,-1,2,4,6]
Sorted union: 1 2 3 4 5 6; the lower middle is 3, then 1 on the left (with 2 as its right child) and 5 on the right (with 4 and 6 as children).

Example 2

a = [2,1], b = [2,-1,3]
Output: [2,1,3]
constraints: 0 ≤ nodes in each tree ≤ 2,500, and at least one node in total
0 ≤ node value ≤ 100,000; both trees are valid BSTs with distinct values inside each tree
The two trees may share values
hints: Converting a BST to a sorted list is easy. What does that suggest for combining two of them?
Take the inorder traversal of each tree, merge the two sorted lists like in merge sort, and skip duplicate values.
Build the balanced tree from the merged sorted list by repeatedly picking the lower middle of a range as root. Use index ranges, not list slices, and serialize level by level.
editorial: An inorder traversal of a BST yields its values in increasing order. Two sorted lists can be merged in linear time with two pointers; while merging, a value equal to the last one written is simply skipped, which removes values that occur in both trees.

The merged list is then turned into a balanced BST exactly as for a sorted array: the middle element becomes the root and both halves are built recursively, which keeps the height at about log<sub>2</sub> n. Total time O(n + m) for the traversals, the merge, the construction and the output; extra space O(n + m).
